structured.approach: I read the DS-05 inputs (task.components at f956a35, feat.design, feat.stories, org.engineering_stack, org.lessons) and the repository's ci.py and CLAUDE.md with the Read tool. I implemented the minimum design from task.components: CMP-1, a new risk.py with vendor_risk; CMP-2, the __init__ export and a minor version step; CMP-3, an additive risk=None last parameter in explain.py. Each has docstrings stating its rules, boundaries and the no-LLM constraint. I documented the changes in docs/ap_forecast.md and README.md. task.code.md states only what tool:repo, ci.py and the inputs support: the gate definitions, and the fact that the current tests never execute the new vendor_risk body or the risk append. The CI result is left to the spine's own record of the run. I also ran /usr/bin/python3 ci.py myself; its outcome is reported in the open questions. I did not inflate coverage with workarounds, did not edit tests/ (outside this step's paths) and did not commit or push.
tools_used: Bash (/usr/bin/python3 ci.py, git status, git diff)

claims.text: New module src/ap_forecast/risk.py defines HIGH_ABOVE_DAYS = 30, MEDIUM_ABOVE_DAYS = 10 and vendor_risk(history), which returns 'high' above 30, 'medium' above 10, else 'low' using strict > on predict_delay_days, and imports only .predict (not explain).
build_explanation_request takes risk=None as its last parameter and appends ' Risk level: <risk>.' to the prompt only when risk is not None; load_config and the returned keys are unchanged.
__init__.py adds vendor_risk to __all__ and takes the minor version step from 0.9.0 that CMP-2 requires.
The package version string in src/ap_forecast/__init__.py is now "0.10.0".
predict.py, models.json and tests/ were left unchanged, as task.components requires.
ci.py enforces COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0 and static checks (no print/eval/exec, no bare except, lines of at most 140 characters) over src/ap_forecast/*.py.

No existing test in tests/test_forecast.py calls vendor_risk or passes risk, so the vendor_risk body and the risk append are not executed by the current suite; test_request_with_explicit_config still calls build_explanation_request with a positional config.
The tests that would cover the new behaviour (CMP-4 tests/test_risk.py and CMP-5 in tests/test_forecast.py) are in tests/, outside the paths this step may change (src/ap_forecast/, docs/, README.md).
No secret, database or new dependency is needed; models.json holds only provider, model and max_tokens.
Existing public signatures are kept and new behaviour is added, as the repository rule requires.
L-007 is reflected: a prediction of exactly 30 gives 'medium' and exactly 10 gives 'low'.

open_questions: CQ-DS5-1: The current suite does not execute the new vendor_risk body or the risk append, so the coverage gate (COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0) depends on the CMP-4 and CMP-5 tests in tests/, which DS-05 may not write. When I ran /usr/bin/python3 ci.py in this step, the coverage gate was not met (overall passed: false), while compile, the 3 existing tests and static checks passed; the spine's CI record holds the exact figures. Confirm DS-06 adds the tests and re-runs CI before DS-07 commits, or allow DS-05 to write tests/.
CQ-DS-2: the next version after 0.9.0 is set as a minor step in __init__.py; Developer to confirm the value.
CQ-DS-1 (carried): risk tests go in a new tests/test_risk.py (TKQ-2); Developer to confirm.
Carried: TQ-8 and PQ-5 gate the release of STORY-04 (sending the risk label to the provider); TQ-4, PQ-1 and TQ-5 are implemented as their interim answers.
structured.summary: I implemented STORY-03 and STORY-04 in ap_forecast: a new rule-based vendor_risk (risk.py, no LLM path), an additive risk=None parameter on build_explanation_request, the vendor_risk export and a minor version step. README.md and a new docs/ap_forecast.md document them. CI does not pass yet: the coverage gate fails because no existing test exercises the new code, and those tests belong in tests/, which this step may not edit; DS-06 will add them. Nothing is committed.
